Ensure that staff are educated that handwashing sinks should ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There were cans of cheese sauce that were observed to be in a hot holding cabinet. The employee stated that they put them in there to make it easier for the cheese sauce to come out. The hot holding cabinet has an ambient temperature of 136F, which is essentially cooking the cheese sauce in the can. Cans are not meant to be used as a cooking vessel, as they have a plastic liner in them that can expose the cheese sauce to adulteration when heated up. CORRECTED- The cans were removed from the hot holding cabinet and it was discussed to put the cheese sauce in containers to cook them in the future. Ensure that food packages are in good condition to protect the food from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There was a box of raw ribeyes on the top shelf of a cooler, above a container of ready-to-eat sauce. CORRECTED- The box of ribeyes was moved to the bottom of the cooler. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
The following TCS food items were observed to be stored past the 7-day date-marking:

1. Orange juice with a use-by date of 10/12/2026. 
2. A container of creamy horseradish portioned cups (made in-house) with a make date of 10/13/2026. 
3. A container of Cajun ranch (made in-house) with a make date of 10/13/2026. 
4. A container of cooked grits with a make date of 10/19/2026. 
5. A container of Au Jus with a make date of 10/13/2026. 
6. A container of maid-rite meat with a make date of 10/18/2026. 
7. A container of bean salad with a make date of 10/18/2026. 

CORRECTED- These items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that TCS food items that are prepared or opened in-house are discarded or used within 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
The following TCS foods were observed to not be date-marked:

1. The milk in the outside bar that was opened Sunday. 
2. The milk in the clear double-door cooler that was opened yesterday. 
3. The tamales in the clear double-cooler that were pulled from the freezer two days ago. 
4. The lettuce in the clear double-door cooler that was prepared yesterday. 
5. The various flavored creamers that were opened on Sunday. 

CORRECTED- The PIC dated the items during the inspection. Ensure that TCS foods that are opened or prepared in-house and are held for more than 24 hours are date-marked, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded or used by the end of the 7th day.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The facility uses ice baths during lunch for TCS food items on the cook-line. The ice bath for sauces only reached a quarter of the way up the bottles of sauces. The ice bath for burger toppings (lettuce, tomatoes, and pickles) and other food items, such as coleslaw, was only ice and only touched the bottom of the container. Coleslaw probed to be at 51.9F and ranch probed to be at 52F. The burger toppings probed to be at 49F. These ice baths had been made at 11am. The PIC stated that they checked the temperatures of the food items at 12pm and that they were under 41F. The PIC stated that the sauces and coleslaw are discarded after four hours and that the other items are placed back in the cooler. Ensure that ice baths are properly submerging the bottom of the containers and are a mixture of both ice and water to allow for proper cold holding. These TCS food items need to be maintained at 41F or below unless they will be under Time as Control and discarded after four hours. CORRECTED- A proper ice bath was discussed with the PIC and the TCS items on the line were placed under Time as Control. These items were discarded at 4pm. Ensure that TCS food items are being properly cold held at 41F or below.

findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
There was beef observed to be stored above 2 lobster tails in the small black cooler along the server line. CORRECTED- The operator switched the storage order of these. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by being in the proper storage order. Proper storage order is as follows: 
1. RTE foods (such as vegetables). 
2. Unwashed vegetables. 
3. Seafood. 
4. Whole cuts of beef and pork.
5. Ground beef and pork. 
6. Whole and ground poultry.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair:

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: Facility was unable to product the Norovirus clean-up policy. Provided during the inspection. See that staff keeps available the Norovirus clean-up policy, sick policy, and reporting agreements. 
A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.comment: 3-304.14: (A) Observed in use wiping clothes stored on food prep surfaces, not in sanitizer solution.  Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: 4-903.11: (A) Observed boxes of to-go containers stored directly on the floor in soda dispensing room.  clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Observed the chlorine concentration in the kitchen dish machine rinse cycle to test at 0 ppm chlorine. A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114.
